style.vernacular: Traditional Bhutanese architecture is mandated by regulation: whitewashed rammed-earth or masonry walls, multi-coloured painted timber frontages and windows with trefoil (arched) tops, small windows on lower floors and larger ones above, and gently sloping roofs in metal sheet, with red ochre bands under the eaves on monastic buildings. Buildings are mostly three storeys or lower. The city lies in a narrow valley at 2,300 m with blue pines on the slopes, prayer flags and mani walls.
style.ornament: Painted wooden window frames with trefoil arched tops, multi-coloured timber frontages with dragon, lotus and cloud motifs, red ochre band with gold roundels below the eaves, gilded finials on roof corners, prayer wheels (mani), prayer flags on poles and chorten shapes.

sources.what: Dzongs and everyday buildings: rammed earth with lime wash, small lower windows with trefoil motifs, steeply sloped roofs of shingle shifting to metal, red upper-wall stripes and gilded copper roofs, 1998 decree requiring multicoloured wood frontages and small arched windows
By regulation all buildings are in traditional style with Buddhist paintings and motifs; narrow valley along the Wang Chhu with conifers, prayer flags and mani walls
High inward-sloping white walls of brick and stone, broad red ochre band, flared roofs now mostly corrugated iron, central tower
